newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian leaders hail Clinton's re-election.
newsitem.headline: Austrian leaders hail Clinton's re-election.

text.p: Austrian leaders congratulated U.S. President Bill Clinton on Wednesday on his re-election, calling his widely expected victory a signal for continuity in U.S. foreign and security policy.

"The vote of the American people is an important sign of continuity in U.S. foreign and security policy, particularly in Bosnia, and of the continuation of joint efforts to create international peace," President Thomas Klestil said.

Klestil, still recovering from a bout of acute pneumonia that confined him to a Vienna hospital for seven weeks until his release on Friday, added that he hoped the continued upswing of the U.S. economy would provide a stimulus for an economic upturn in Austria and the rest of Europe.
Social Democratic Chancellor Franz Vranitzky also applauded Clinton's victory, but added that the U.S. president now faced a number of key social and economic challenges.
"I hope the U.S. will contribute to a consistent economic policy in terms of unemployment, social security, and high environmental standards," he told Austrian state television.

He added that Russian President Boris Yeltsin's successful heart operation should put the Russian leader "very soon in a position to contribute to the peaceful cooperation of the two big powers to guarantee an orderly development of the world".
